title: Morning preview
tomorrow: a young man walks into a river at dawn and doesn't come out. then?

segments.voice: That was a week of mornings: the first minute given before the crowd, breath before phone, my morning line, today I will, move first, and yesterday, glad to wake, for a soul given back. One piece left before the whole morning comes together.

Your calendar already knows who you'll see today, the easy meeting and the hard one. Marcus Aurelius, emperor of Rome, kept a private notebook we now call the Meditations, and one entry opens like a warning to himself: "Begin the morning by saying to thyself, I shall meet with the busy-body, the ungrateful, arrogant, deceitful, envious, unsocial." An emperor, listing who's going to annoy him. Why start a day that way?
screen: `THE EASY MEETING AND THE HARD ONE.` → `AN EMPEROR'S NOTEBOOK.` → `I SHALL MEET WITH THE BUSY-BODY.`

segments.voice: Because of what comes next: "All these things happen to them by reason of their ignorance of what is good and evil." Marcus was a Stoic, and in the same entry he says none of them can injure him, because no one can drag him into what is ugly. For him, the only real harm is harm to his own character. So the rude person can't truly injure him. And he can't hate them either, because, he says, they are his kin, sharing in the same reason. Then the picture: "For we are made for co-operation, like feet, like hands, like eyelids, like the rows of the upper and lower teeth." That's the teaching: the Stoic morning preview. You rehearse the hard people before you meet them, not to brace for a fight, but so you've already chosen how you'll act, as one hand working with another. Notice he doesn't pretend everyone will be pleasant. He expects the difficult ones and decides on kindness in advance. That's the line between a preview and a worry. A worry rehearses the bad scene. A preview rehearses you, at your best, inside it.
screen: `THEY DON'T KNOW GOOD FROM EVIL.` · `NO ONE CAN HARM YOUR CHARACTER.` · `MADE FOR CO-OPERATION, LIKE HANDS.` · `A PREVIEW, NOT A WORRY.` · then, large: `I'LL MEET THEM KINDLY.`

segments.voice: Walk through today in order, and stop at the person you're least looking forward to. Picture the moment you'll meet them, and picture yourself meeting them kindly, the way Marcus decided before his day began. Then let the picture go and rest in a few slow breaths.
Morning preview: meeting the day's hard people in your mind first, and choosing kindness before you get there. The Stoic preview of Marcus Aurelius.
Hold on to this: I'll meet them kindly, like hand with hand. A week of mornings, done.
